exposure: prolonged pregnancy (42 weeks of gestation or more)
outcome: maternal complications (cesarean delivery, perineal tears, forceps delivery)
fetal complications (macrosomia, pathological FHR during labor, fetal distress)
cohort: 50 women who gave birth at 42 weeks of gestation or more at the Maternity of the Farhat Hached University Hospital Center in Sousse.
finding: Prolonged pregnancy (≥42 WG) significantly increases the risk of maternal and fetal complications, and systematic induction of labor at 41 WG is recommended to reduce these adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: Maternal complications of prolonged pregnancy included increased rates of cesarean delivery (48%) and forceps delivery (20%).
